decisions.rejectedArgument: Supporting only CPython 3.13.15 is a defect merely because a newer Python minor exists.
decisions.scope: The current company-aligned runtime support projection, not dependency security or runtime correctness.
assumptions: The owner still selects the singleton company runtime.
Required dependencies remain compatible with this runtime; security qualification is checked separately.
protectedObservations: One exact runtime identity agrees across package, container, development and CI projections.
decisions.simplestAlternative: Support additional Python minors and validate every added runtime independently.
decisions.rationale: Additional runtime families add a compatibility obligation without an admitted consumer need. A higher version number alone establishes no benefit under this scope.
decisions.acceptedCost: Newer-runtime capabilities and optimizations are not automatically available.
falsifiers: An applicable security advisory or required dependency cannot be handled on the admitted runtime.
A required workload has a demonstrated unacceptable limitation that an admitted newer runtime resolves.
revisionTriggers: Security support, dependency compatibility or a measured workload budget changes.
decisions.residualReview: Always review exact patch security, dependency compatibility and projection consistency; this decision is not a security exception.

decisions.rejectedArgument: The ledger-head lock is intrinsically an architecture bug and should be replaced with per-repository chains.
decisions.scope: The current complete-ledger total-order and paired-state audit contract, not the measured cost of its implementation.
assumptions: One retained total order remains an owner requirement.
No measured capacity result proves the current serialization budget unacceptable.
protectedObservations: Subject filtering cannot hide corruption elsewhere in the frozen chain.
An audit event and its owning state transition commit atomically.
decisions.simplestAlternative: Partition audit order by repository with a new cross-chain verification and checkpoint contract.
decisions.rationale: Partitioning changes the proof relation rather than preserving the same contract faster. Such a transition needs explicit owner admission and witnesses.
decisions.acceptedCost: Audit appends serialize on the ledger head; throughput and contention still require measurement.
falsifiers: A reachable deadlock or excessive lock duration violates the admitted lifecycle.
Measured representative load exceeds the capacity budget.
revisionTriggers: The audit owner no longer requires one total order.
Contention measurements or deployment topology justify a versioned alternative.
decisions.residualReview: Review lock ordering, transaction duration, cancellation, throughput, retention and checkpoint integrity. Do not report capacity as proved by this record.

decisions.rejectedArgument: Canonical audit payload text should unconditionally be replaced by JSONB because JSONB is the modern PostgreSQL JSON type.
decisions.scope: The durable byte identity used by audit hashing and replay, not auxiliary analytical projections.
assumptions: Prepared canonical payload bytes remain authoritative for the retained hash.
Queries do not require replacing that byte authority with normalized database JSON.
protectedObservations: Persistence writes the exact prepared payload used to derive its hash, without rereading or recanonicalizing caller data.
decisions.simplestAlternative: Retain canonical bytes and add a separately owned bounded query projection only when needed.
decisions.rationale: A storage-type preference does not establish equivalence of byte identity. A query projection can preserve the original authority without redefining replay.
decisions.acceptedCost: Arbitrary JSON queries may require decoding or an additional justified projection.
falsifiers: Stored bytes differ from the prepared hash input.
Parsing, payload limits or query cost violate a required budget.
revisionTriggers: An analytical consumer or schema evolution changes access needs.
The canonical format or replay owner changes.
decisions.residualReview: Continue checking canonicalization, Unicode, parser bounds, SQL storage constraints and query cost; this is not a blanket exemption for text JSON.

decisions.rejectedArgument: A file is a blockable god-file solely because its line count, exports or fan-out exceed a threshold.
decisions.scope: Metric-only severity assignment under the current repository module-ownership policy.
assumptions: The finding provides only selection metrics, not a closed forbidden-coownership proof.
protectedObservations: Production and test cohorts remain distinct.
Real boundary defects remain reviewable even in small files.
decisions.simplestAlternative: Use size thresholds as review-selection signals, then prove semantic ownership and a safe preferable decomposition.
decisions.rationale: Size is neither necessary nor sufficient for forbidden semantic coownership. It cannot discharge the profile's remaining predicates.
decisions.acceptedCost: Semantic candidate review remains a human or agent evidence task; not every large file will be split.
falsifiers: The finding supplies applicable ownership, exact epoch, observables, a complete safe preferable decomposition and the remaining block predicates.
revisionTriggers: New ownership evidence, changed responsibilities or changed repository policy.
decisions.residualReview: Always inspect selected candidates for real concentration, fragmentation, naming and risk. This record rejects the size-only inference, not decomposition.

decisions.rejectedArgument: The service requires an internal broker, separate CQRS database or microservices solely to qualify as an enterprise architecture.
decisions.scope: Internal deployment boundaries of the current modular monolith; external provider recovery is a separate obligation.
assumptions: One deployable backend and transactional database still satisfy the admitted context.
No independent internal consumer or deployment boundary has been required.
protectedObservations: Local state and audit changes remain atomic.
Provider timeout, ambiguity and recovery remain explicit rather than treated as local calls.
decisions.simplestAlternative: Use cohesive modules, existing transaction boundaries and bounded provider reconciliation.
decisions.rationale: Extra distributed boundaries add partial failure and operational obligations without an evidenced independent consumer. Popularity does not demonstrate net benefit.
decisions.acceptedCost: Internal capabilities share deployment and database failure domains.
falsifiers: Required independent scaling, failure isolation, governance or deployment cannot be satisfied inside the current boundary.
A missing recovery contract is incorrectly defended as a monolith choice.
revisionTriggers: Independent consumers, ownership or hard operational budgets change.
decisions.residualReview: Continue reviewing modularity, workload isolation, durable recovery and database availability; this decision does not excuse a dropped delivery or unbounded queue.
